q: You buy bread at a ___.
explain: A bakery makes and sells bread and cakes.

q: I feel ___. I need to go to bed.
explain: When you're tired, you need sleep.

q: The opposite of 'cheap' is ___.
A person who serves food in a restaurant is a ___.
explain: A waiter serves; a chef cooks.

q: Can you ___ me some money? I'll pay you back.
explain: You LEND to someone; you BORROW from someone.

q: I ___ my homework every evening.
We ___ a photo of the castle.
The train was ___, so we arrived late.
Which one is a vegetable?
explain: A carrot is a vegetable; the others are fruit.

q: Put on your ___ — it's raining!
My mother's brother is my ___.
explain: Your parent's brother is your uncle.

q: I'm very ___ in history. I love old castles.
explain: People FEEL interested; things ARE interesting.

q: Could you ___ the window? It's hot in here.
explain: When it's hot, open the window.

q: The film was really ___. I laughed a lot.
A ___ is where you can see old and interesting things.
explain: Museums show old and interesting things.

q: I need to ___ the bus at the next stop.
explain: Get off = leave a bus or train.

q: Turn ___ the light, please. It's dark.
explain: When it's dark, turn ON the light.

q: I'm ___. Can I have a glass of water?
We ___ our holiday in Scotland last year.
Don't forget to ___ your teeth before bed.
The shop ___ at six o'clock, so hurry!
A ___ is a doctor for animals.
explain: A vet looks after sick animals.

q: I can't find my glasses. Can you help me ___ for them?
The opposite of 'noisy' is ___.
He ___ a cold, so he stayed at home.
Which one do you wear on your hands in winter?
Can I ___ on this dress? — Yes, the changing room is there.
explain: try on = put clothes on to see if they fit.

q: It's very ___ today. Hold on to your hat!
My grandma is ___. She's 92!
explain: 'Elderly' is a polite word for old.

q: Please ___ the form and give it back to me.
explain: fill in a form = write the information.

q: I'd like to ___ a table for two at eight.
